chunks.arabic_text: رِجَالُ الْكَشِّيِّ: حَمْدَوَيْهَ وَمُحَمَّدٌ، عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى، عَنْ صَفْوَانَ، عَنْ عَبْدِ الرَّحْمَنِ بْنِ الْحَجَّاجِ قَالَ

translations.en: Rijal al-Kashshi: Hamduwayh and Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Safwan, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj who said:

chunks.arabic_text: سَأَلَ أَبُوعَبَّاسَ فَضْلُ الْبَقْبَاقِ لِحَرِيزَ الْإِذْنَ عَلَى أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ فَلَمْ يُؤْذِنْ لَهُ، فَعَاوَدَهُ فَلَمْ يُؤْذِنْ لَهُ، فَقَالَ: أَيُّ شَيْءٍ لِلرَّجُلِ أَنْ يَبْلُغَ مِنْ عُقُوبَةِ غُلَامِهِ؟ قَالَ: عَلَى قَدْرِ ذُنُوبِهِ، فَقَالَ: قَدْ عَاقَبْتُ وَ اللَّهِ حَرِيزًا بِأَعْظَمَ مِمَّا صَنَعَ، قَالَ: وَيْحَكَ إِنِّي فَعَلْتُ؟ ذَلِكَ أَنَّ حَرِيزًا جَرَّدَ السَّيْفَ! ثُمَّ قَالَ: أَمَا لَوْ كَانَ حُذَيْفَةُ بْنُ مَنْصُورٍ مَا عَاوَدَنِي فِيهِ بَعْدَ أَنْ قُلْتُ لَا

translations.en: Abu al-Abbas Fadl al-Baqbaq sought permission for Hariz to enter upon Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) but he was not granted permission, so he repeated the request but was not granted permission, so he said: What extent should a man reach in punishing his slave? He said: According to his sins, he said: I have punished Hariz by Allah with greater than what he did, he said: Woe to you! Am I the one who did that? That is because Hariz unsheathed the sword! Then he said: If it were Hudhayfa ibn Mansur, he would not have persisted in the request after I had said no.

en.summary: This narration from Al-Kashi’s *Rijal* highlights the Imam’s discernment in distinguishing between minor infractions and serious breaches of protocol, using the specific act of unsheathing a sword to justify the severity of the punishment. The Imam’s comparison with Hudhayfa ibn Mansur, known for his patience and composure, serves as a scholarly lesson on how one’s character and demeanor influence their standing and interactions with the Imams. It underscores the Shia emphasis on *adab* (etiquette) and the nuanced understanding of authority within the Ahl al-Bayt's circle.
en.seo_question: What was the reason for Imam al-Sadiq's refusal to grant permission to Hariz and his reaction to Fadl's complaint?

key_terms.فَضْلُ الْبَقْبَاقِ: Fadl al-Baqbaq, a companion of the Imams
key_terms.حَرِيز: Hariz, a slave or servant of Fadl al-Baqbaq
key_terms.جَرَّدَ السَّيْفَ: Unsheathed the sword, indicating a serious or aggressive act
key_terms.حُذَيْفَةُ بْنُ مَنْصُورٍ: Hudhayfa ibn Mansur, a known companion known for patience
